description: Use when designing or maintaining the role hierarchy as a record-access mechanism. Trigger keywords: role hierarchy, manager cannot see subordinate records, grant access using hierarchies, role reparenting, portal role, how deep should the role hierarchy be, design the role hierarchy. NOT for territory models - use admin/enterprise-territory-management. NOT for rule-based grants - use admin/sharing-rules. NOT for the overall model - use admin/sharing-and-visibility.
inputs: Org-wide defaults per object: the hierarchy only grants anything where OWD is Private or Public Read Only
Which access requirements are vertical (manager sees subordinate) versus horizontal (peer sees peer)
Existing role count and the org's creation date, which decides the 500 vs 5,000 role ceiling
Whether Experience Cloud / partner or customer portal accounts exist, and who owns them
Whether any user owns more than 10,000 records of a single object (ownership skew)
Planned maintenance window, because role reparenting blocks almost all other group updates
name: role-hierarchy-design
official_sources: Salesforce Security Guide (Spring '26) — https://resources.docs.salesforce.com/262/latest/en-us/sfdc/pdf/salesforce_security_impl_guide.pdf — source for "Create a User Role" (the two documented exceptions to upward inheritance; the account-child access step; the `View Roles and Role Hierarchy` / `Manage Roles` / `Manage Internal Users` permissions and the Professional–Developer edition list), "Organization-Wide Sharing Defaults" (Grant Access Using Hierarchies editable for custom objects only and not when default access is Controlled by Parent; Account-Private forcing Opportunity/Case to Private; asynchronous recalculation and the completion email), "Sharing Rules" (hierarchy propagation of rule-granted access; the Roles / Portal Roles / Roles and Internal Subordinates member categories and the February 8, 2024 availability split; high-volume site users having no role), "Public and Personal Groups" (the group-level Grant Access Using Hierarchies option and the All Internal Users optimisation), and the Setup Audit Trail coverage of the option. Also available page-by-page at https://developer.salesforce.com/docs/atlas.en-us.securityImplGuide.meta/securityImplGuide/admin_roles.htm (`admin_sharing.htm`, `users_group_member_types.htm`, `creating_and_editing_groups.htm`, `security_sharing_rule_considerations.htm`, `admin_monitorsetup.htm`), which is the form each quotation above was re-verified against on 2026-08-15.

Salesforce Spring '21 Release Notes — https://resources.docs.salesforce.com/230/latest/en-us/sfdc/pdf/salesforce_spring21_release_notes.pdf — "Create More Roles": the 5,000-role ceiling for orgs created in Spring '21 or later, the 500-role default for older orgs, the Customer Support escalation path, and the guidance to set up roles based on data access. The PDF was downloaded and the section read directly on 2026-08-15; the wording is verbatim "In Salesforce orgs created in Spring '21 or later, you can create up to 5,000 roles. In existing orgs, the default limit hasn't changed. You can create up to 500 roles and can contact Salesforce Customer Support to increase this limit."

Record-Level Access: Under the Hood (Spring '26) — https://developer.salesforce.com/docs/atlas.en-us.salesforce_record_access_under_the_hood.meta/salesforce_record_access_under_the_hood/uth_grants.htm for the four access-grant types; `.../uth_arch.htm` for the Object Record / Object Sharing / Group Maintenance table split, the statement that Object Sharing tables "store the data that supports explicit and implicit grants", and the rule that an object gets no Object Sharing table when both org-wide defaults are Public Read/Write; `.../uth_groups.htm` for the `Role` / `RoleAndSubordinates` / `RoleAndSubordinatesInternal` system-defined groups created "depending on if digital experiences is enabled" (the availability note is on `RoleAndSubordinates`) and for direct versus indirect membership; `.../uth_putting_it_all_together.htm` for the "1–3 roles are appended to the main hierarchy below the account owner's role" figure and the full accounting of a user role change. Verified 2026-08-15 page by page — the 1–3 figure is in "Putting It All Together", not in the group-maintenance chapter.

Designing Record Access for Enterprise Scale (Spring '26) — https://resources.docs.salesforce.com/latest/latest/en-us/sfdc/pdf/draes.pdf — the full accounting of what a user role change performs, the cost of moving a whole role, the ownership-data-skew definition (a single user owning more than 10,000 records of an object) and its three-part mitigation, group membership locking with the verbatim "could not acquire lock" and "Group membership operation already in progress" error strings, and the granular-locking concurrency table showing that reparenting blocks almost all other group updates while a role delete blocks only a small subset. Re-verified 2026-08-15 against the HTML edition at https://developer.salesforce.com/docs/atlas.en-us.draes.meta/draes/draes_group_membership.htm (`draes_group_membership_data_skew.htm`, `draes_group_membership_locking.htm`).

Best Practices for Deployments with Large Data Volumes — https://resources.docs.salesforce.com/latest/latest/en-us/sfdc/pdf/salesforce_large_data_volumes_bp.pdf — "Avoid having any user own more than 10,000 records", and the load ordering that populates roles before sharing rules and adds sharing rules one at a time. Re-verified 2026-08-15 against https://developer.salesforce.com/docs/atlas.en-us.salesforce_large_data_volumes_bp.meta/salesforce_large_data_volumes_bp/ldv_deployments_best_practices_general.htm and `ldv_deployments_best_practices_api_loading_data.htm`.

Metadata API Developer Guide: Role — https://developer.salesforce.com/docs/atlas.en-us.api_meta.meta/api_meta/meta_role.htm — `parentRole` ("The role above this role in the hierarchy"), the `.role` suffix, the `roles` directory, and availability from API version 24.0. Verified 2026-08-15.

Metadata API Developer Guide: RoleOrTerritory — https://developer.salesforce.com/docs/atlas.en-us.api_meta.meta/api_meta/meta_roleorterritory.htm — `caseAccessLevel`, `contactAccessLevel`, `opportunityAccessLevel` with valid values `Read` / `Edit` / `None`, the conditions under which each is hidden, and `mayForecastManagerShare`. Verified 2026-08-15.

Metadata API Developer Guide: CustomObject — https://developer.salesforce.com/docs/atlas.en-us.api_meta.meta/api_meta/customobject.htm — confirms the type exposes `sharingModel` and `externalSharingModel` and has no field representing Grant Access Using Hierarchies, which is the basis for the "it does not deploy" guidance. Verified 2026-08-15.

Object Reference: UserRole — https://developer.salesforce.com/docs/atlas.en-us.object_reference.meta/object_reference/sforce_api_objects_role.htm — the field list (`ParentRoleId`, `CaseAccessForAccountOwner`, `ContactAccessForAccountOwner`, `OpportunityAccessForAccountOwner` marked Required with "you can't set a user role with an opportunity access less than that specified in organization-wide defaults", `ContactAccessForAccountOwner` non-writable when `DefaultContactAccess` is Controlled by Parent, `ForecastUserId`, `RollupDescription`, `MayForecastManagerShare`, `PortalType`, `PortalRole`, `PortalAccountId`, `PortalAccountOwnerId`, `DeveloperName`, `IsPartner`), the access rule "only users with the View Roles and Role Hierarchy permission can access this object, and only users with the Manage Roles permission can edit this object", and the verbatim "You can't update any field for a portal role." Verified against the current version on 2026-08-15.

Object Reference: Group — https://developer.salesforce.com/docs/atlas.en-us.object_reference.meta/object_reference/sforce_api_objects_group.htm — `DoesIncludeBosses` ("Indicates whether records shared with users in this group are also shared with users higher in the role hierarchy... This field is only available for groups of type Regular and Queue... corresponds to the Grant Access Using Hierarchies checkbox on the detail pages of public groups and queues"; API 18.0+ for Regular, 67.0+ for Queue), `RelatedId` ("For groups of type 'Role,' the ID of the associated UserRole"), and the `Type` picklist. This page independently confirms the availability split the skill relies on: `RoleAndSubordinates` is "Only available when digital experiences is enabled for your org and Experience Cloud site users are created with external account roles other than a shared person account role", while `RoleAndSubordinatesInternal` carries no such gate. Verified against the current version on 2026-08-15.

Object Reference: AccountShare — https://developer.salesforce.com/docs/atlas.en-us.object_reference.meta/object_reference/sforce_api_objects_accountshare.htm — the `RowCause` picklist, introduced with "Valid values include" and listing fourteen causes (`Manual`, `Owner`, `Team`, `Rule`, `GuestRule`, `ImplicitParent`, `GuestParentImplicit`, `LpuParentImplicit`, `LpuImplicit`, `PortalImplicit`, `ARImplicit`, `Territory`, `Territory2AssociationManual`, and the deprecated `TerritoryManual`); the row-compression rule for `ImplicitParent` / `Manual` / `Owner`; and "For some sharing mechanisms, such as sharing sets, sharing entries aren't stored at all", with the accompanying warning not to build customizations that rely on share rows existing. Recorded **with those qualifiers** because the skill deliberately does not argue from the picklist's contents that a hierarchy cause is absent — that claim rests on the Object Sharing / Group Maintenance table split instead. Verified against the current version on 2026-08-15; an earlier draft of this skill cited an archived (192.0) copy of the page whose four-value list is long out of date.

Object Reference (entry point) — https://developer.salesforce.com/docs/atlas.en-us.object_reference.meta/object_reference/sforce_api_objects_concepts.htm — the canonical index used to locate `UserRole`, `Group`, and `AccountShare`.

Metadata API Developer Guide (entry point) — https://developer.salesforce.com/docs/atlas.en-us.api_meta.meta/api_meta/meta_intro.htm — the canonical index used to locate `Role`, `RoleOrTerritory`, and `CustomObject`.

Salesforce Security Guide: Restriction Rules — https://developer.salesforce.com/docs/atlas.en-us.securityImplGuide.meta/securityImplGuide/security_restriction_rule.htm — "Restriction rules are available for custom objects, external objects, contracts, events, quotes, tasks, time sheets, and time sheet entries", plus the two-active-rules (Enterprise, Developer) and five-active-rules (Performance, Unlimited) per-object counts. This is the source that rules restriction rules OUT as a workaround for Account, Opportunity, Case, Contact and Lead. Verified 2026-08-15.

Salesforce Security Guide: Sharing Rule Considerations and User Sharing Considerations — https://developer.salesforce.com/docs/atlas.en-us.securityImplGuide.meta/securityImplGuide/security_sharing_rule_considerations.htm and `.../security_sharing_users_concept.htm` — "Users in the role hierarchy are automatically granted the same access that users below them in the hierarchy have from a sharing rule provided that the object is a standard object or the Grant Access Using Hierarchies option is selected if the object is a custom object", and "the user records of high-volume users, Chatter External, and Chatter Free users can't be included in sharing rules, and these users can't be granted access to user records via a sharing rule." Verified 2026-08-15.
Salesforce Well-Architected Overview — https://architect.salesforce.com/docs/architect/well-architected/guide/overview.html — pillar framing for the sections above.
outputs: A role hierarchy design keyed to record-access requirements, not to the org chart
Deployable `Role` metadata with parentRole and the three account-child access levels set
A Grant Access Using Hierarchies decision per custom object, with the Controlled by Parent exclusions called out
A role-change runbook covering recalculation, locking, and portal-role side effects
A list of access requirements that the hierarchy cannot satisfy, routed to sharing rules, territories, or Apex managed sharing
